misconceptions.description: Polishing individual frames well but never checking that the full storyboard tells one coherent instructional sequence toward the objective
misconceptions.trigger: learner perfects single frames but the storyboard has gaps or repeats across the sequence
misconceptions.feedback: A studio submission is the whole sequence. Trace the objective across all frames; strong frames that do not connect still fail the storyboard.

misconceptions.description: Applying a multimedia principle on one frame but contradicting it elsewhere in the same storyboard
misconceptions.trigger: learner segments one frame but lets a later frame auto-advance through dense content
misconceptions.feedback: Apply each principle consistently across the storyboard. A principle honored on Frame 2 and broken on Frame 6 signals an unintegrated design.

misconceptions.description: Treating the studio capstone as collecting the module's separate artifacts rather than integrating them into one defensible storyboard with an evidence trail
misconceptions.trigger: learner staples together earlier exercises with no integrating rationale
misconceptions.feedback: The studio integrates, it does not collect. Show how the frames, modality, accessibility, and review decisions serve one objective.

misconceptions.description: Submitting a final storyboard with no record of the major design decisions, rejected options, and the evidence behind them
misconceptions.trigger: learner submits the polished storyboard alone with no decision log
misconceptions.feedback: The capstone needs its evidence trail: key decisions, what was rejected, and the principle or learner data behind each choice.

misconceptions.description: Accepting an AI-suggested addition (such as a bonus frame) because it looks good or enriches the content, rather than because it serves the storyboard's single objective.
misconceptions.trigger: learner keeps an AI-suggested frame that introduces a second objective into the sequence
misconceptions.feedback: Run the objective trace on every AI suggestion: a frame that does not serve the one stated objective dilutes the sequence, however polished it is. Integration is mostly subtraction; cut the addition and record the rejection with its reason in the decision record.
